docs.title: Wonder Kingdom Wiki
docs.text: Wonder Kingdom is a MapleStory-like open-world platformer RPG built with GameLib. This wiki covers its world, its story and everything you can find, fight and make in it.

docs.title: Where things come from
docs.text:
• Lore is written here. This wiki is the source of truth for the story, the history and the people of Wonder Kingdom.
  • Game data (items, skills, jobs, monsters, bosses, NPCs, quests, maps, professions) is generated from the game's content files in GameLib, which is the source of truth for how the game plays. Those pages are rebuilt by tools/generate.py, so fix game data in GameLib, not here.

docs.title: The Snail King
docs.text:
A giant snail named Mano sleeps in a hollow past the woods, and it does not like visitors. Watch the red marks: they show where it will land. Potions work in there; scrolls do not.

Boss Mano Arena The Snail King's Hollow

  • Entered by talking to Hale

docs.title: Lore
docs.text:
Wonder Kingdom is a bright, prosperous and genuinely united kingdom on the island of Veligor. Its people come from different cultures and keep different traditions, yet they share a real sense of belonging and respect for one another. Their towns are lively, their markets are full, and their differences are celebrated rather than feared.

It was not always so. Before the kingdom, Veligor was split between four peoples who had fought each other for generations. Only the coming of the Balrog, an ancient being too strong for any one of them, drove them to stand together. They beat it, sealed it beneath the roots of the great World Tree, and founded Wonder Kingdom on the cooperation that won that war.

Fifty years ago, an expedition into the World Tree opened a rift deep beneath its roots and damaged the seal. The Balrog has not escaped, but its influence has been seeping out ever since. Wild creatures have grown aggressive, and the wilderness between the towns has filled with monsters.

The kingdom is still whole and happy. The land around it is turning hostile. That contrast is the heart of the world.

Core premise

Wonder Kingdom is a genuinely happy and united civilization, born from the cooperation of four formerly divided peoples. Generations later, an ancient threat imprisoned beneath the World Tree is slowly returning, and a new generation must protect the peaceful world its ancestors created.

docs.title: The Age of Disturbance
docs.text: The fifty years since the expedition are known as the Age of Disturbance. Through the damaged seal, the Balrog's influence has been creeping out of its prison and across Veligor, and its effects grow harder to ignore every year. Above all, the island's wilderness has become far more dangerous.

docs.title: Wild Creatures Turn Aggressive
docs.text:
Creatures that once kept away from travelers, or simply went about their lives, began attacking anyone who wandered into their territory. Monsters became common in the forests, plains, mountains and caves.

It is not the same everywhere. Some places have seen only small changes, while others have become home to truly dangerous creatures. The towns themselves are still peaceful, but every road between them has grown riskier.

docs.title: The Nature of Monsters
docs.text:
The monsters roaming Veligor are tied to the weakening seal. The spread of the Balrog's influence is why such a peaceful land is now full of hostile creatures.

That does not mean the Balrog commands every one of them. Some are ordinary animals whose nature it has twisted. Others are magical beings changed by a changing land.

docs.title: Life Under the Disturbance
docs.text:
The growing danger in the wilds has made travel, exploration, farming and any work outside the towns harder. Yet Wonder Kingdom carries on. Its towns are still prosperous and welcoming, and its people work together against the threat.

The kingdom has not fallen into fear, hostility or division. The monsters are simply a new challenge, met by a civilization that was already united.

Design notes

"The Age of Disturbance" is a provisional name. Exactly how the Balrog's influence creates or changes monsters is not settled, including whether entirely new creatures can appear.

docs.title: The Great World Tree Expedition
docs.text: Fifty years ago, Wonder Kingdom sent an expedition into the World Tree. The Tree had been a landmark for centuries, but most of its interior had never been explored, and the journey became one of the greatest feats of exploration in the kingdom's history.

docs.title: The Upper Chambers
docs.text:
The explorers first climbed up through the Tree's vast inner passages. They found astonishing magical places: strange plants, extraordinary creatures and natural structures of dizzying complexity.

There they met the Children of the Tree, a magical people who had lived cut off from the rest of the world. After the expedition, the Children gradually moved to Fairy Forest and became part of the wider kingdom.

docs.title: The Discovery of Cavelor
docs.text:
Having explored the heights, the expedition turned downward, into the depths beneath the Tree. There they found Cavelor.

They learned that the descendants of ancient guardians had lived in the hidden city for generations, keeping the memory of the Balrog alive and guarding its prison. The legendary war against the Balrog, it turned out, had left behind a living order sworn to stop its return.

docs.title: The Accident
docs.text:
Exploring the passages deeper still, the explorers accidentally opened a rift, and the rift damaged the magic that held the Balrog.

The seal did not break. It began, very slowly, to weaken. At first nobody realized what had happened. But over the following decades, the failing seal began to reach the world above, and the Age of Disturbance began.

docs.title: The Age of Division
docs.text: Long before Wonder Kingdom, four peoples shared Veligor, and each had its own idea of how life ought to be lived.

docs.title: The Savages
docs.text: The Savages held the rugged wilds and the mountains. They prized strength, endurance and independence, honored their ancestors, and lived close to the land. Their communities were built around survival and cooperation, and respect went to whoever showed courage and perseverance. They fought off every outside authority that tried to rule their territory or press strange customs on them.

docs.title: The Magicians
docs.text: The Magicians gave their lives to understanding the supernatural forces of Veligor, above all the World Tree, the old places where magic ran deep, and the bond between magic and nature. They valued knowledge, magical skill and preservation, and they stood against anyone who tried to exploit or seize the places they held sacred.

docs.title: The Commons
docs.text: The Commons were the farmers, merchants, craftsmen and settlers who kept ordinary life running. They built villages, farms, workshops and trade routes, and they valued cooperation, practical skill, honest work and prosperity. What they wanted most was safety and stability across the island.

docs.title: The Aristocrats
docs.text: The Aristocrats raised fortified settlements, wrote laws and built the first real institutions of government. They believed that order, administration and strong central leadership were the way to a stable and prosperous Veligor.

docs.title: The Ancient Conflict
docs.text:
For generations the island was split into two loose alliances: the Savages and the Magicians on one side, the Commons and the Aristocrats on the other.

They fought over land, over who had the right to rule, over whose traditions should prevail, and over access to the island's most important natural and magical places. The quarrels hardened into long wars. Each side had real strengths, but neither could win a lasting peace, and Veligor never became one civilization.

It took a far greater threat to end it.

docs.title: The Balrog War
docs.text:
The ancient conflict was cut short by the arrival of the Balrog, a being of immense power and destruction.

It threatened every people on the island at once. Settlements burned, armies were broken, and even the mightiest warriors and magicians could barely stand against it. For the first time, all four peoples faced an enemy none of them could beat alone, and next to that danger their old grievances suddenly seemed very small.

So they united, and each gave what it did best:

  • The Savages sent their strongest warriors, whose courage and strength carried the fight to the Balrog itself.
  • The Magicians brought their knowledge of ancient magic, which in the end made it possible to imprison the creature.
  • The Commons gathered supplies, forged equipment and kept the united armies fed and moving.
  • The Aristocrats supplied military organization and leadership, and coordinated the four forces as one.

Together they defeated the Balrog. But it could not be destroyed. Instead, the alliance wove a great magical seal and bound the creature deep within the roots of the World Tree at the heart of Veligor.

That victory ended the Age of Division.

docs.title: The Founding of Wonder Kingdom
docs.text:
After the Balrog was sealed away, the leaders of the four peoples met to make the peace last. They signed a treaty that formally ended their old wars and joined them into a single realm: Wonder Kingdom.

The founding treaty declared that every people of Veligor could live together in peace, whatever their ancestry, culture, station or magical gifts. The kingdom was built on the same cooperation that had won the war.

Over the generations that followed, the four peoples grew a shared identity without giving up their own. Their cultures kept living and changing inside the new kingdom. Towns traded, friendships crossed the old lines, and knowledge passed freely from one community to the next. The old hostilities faded until nobody thought of their neighbors as ancestral enemies anymore. The unity the treaty had promised simply became the way people lived.

docs.title: The Meaning of Unity
docs.text:
Wonder Kingdom is not held together by fear, force or a fragile political bargain. Its unity is real.

Its people understand and value one another across their differences. Each town keeps its own customs and way of life, and those differences are a source of pride rather than friction. Everyone is proud of the shared history and of the civilization their ancestors built. The old wars are remembered as history, but they no longer shape how communities treat each other.

That holds for every settlement on Veligor, including Urbanograd, whose unconventional culture is accepted across the kingdom.

docs.title: Wonder Kingdom Today
docs.text:
Fifty years have passed since the Great World Tree Expedition, and Wonder Kingdom is still peaceful, prosperous and wonderfully diverse.

  • Selsior flourishes as the bustling capital.
  • Kaldemor keeps its cheerful country traditions and its love of craft.
  • Midbarium holds fast to its resilient highland ways.
  • Fairy Forest remains the heart of magic and harmony with nature.
  • Urbanograd, now a century old, still goes its own colorful way.
  • Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour thrive as independent ports with very different characters.
  • Cavelor keeps its ancient watch beneath the World Tree.

docs.title: Everyday Life
docs.text:
For all the danger beyond their walls, the people of Wonder Kingdom live ordinary, happy lives. They trade, farm, craft, learn, play, explore and celebrate. Travel, trade, friendship and shared culture tie the island's communities together, and people are proud to call the kingdom home.

Their happiness is real. It is not a pretty face hiding a broken society.

docs.title: The Dangerous Wilderness
docs.text:
Outside the towns, it is another story. Monsters roam much of Veligor's wilderness, and forests, mountains, plains, caves and ancient ruins have all grown more dangerous. Travelers and adventurers must face aggressive creatures and treacherous ground.

Peaceful towns and a dangerous wild: that contrast is the defining feature of the world.

docs.title: The Forgotten Threat
docs.text:
To most people, the Balrog is a legend, a figure out of history books. It was defeated and locked away so long ago that hardly anyone thinks of it as a danger today.

The people of Cavelor know better. They remember the first war and understand the seal, and they know that its slow failure is a serious threat.

And deep beneath the World Tree, the Balrog's influence keeps spreading.

docs.title: Worldbuilding Principles
docs.text:
These principles guide all future lore. New pages and stories should stay true to them.

  1. Wonder Kingdom is genuinely united. Its communities are not secretly hostile toward one another.
  2. The four original peoples were once divided. Their conflict ended through cooperation against the Balrog and the founding treaty that followed.
  3. Cultural differences still matter. Unity did not erase the traditions or identities of Veligor's communities.
  4. Urbanograd was founded 100 years ago. Its people are rebels in a cultural sense, not political insurgents.
  5. Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour are independent towns. Their resemblance to other towns is cultural and atmospheric, not a sign that anyone governs them.
  6. Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour lie on opposite sides of Veligor. They have different identities without being rivals.
  7. Selsior is the City of Everything. It is a joyful, bustling, cosmopolitan metropolis with classic medieval fantasy architecture.
  8. Kaldemor is the Town of Joyful Craftsmanship. It is a cheerful, prosperous, pastoral community inspired by Henesys.
  9. Midbarium is a rugged, rural highland town ruled by clan chieftains. It stands for strength, resilience, independence and ancestral tradition, and its dry, desert-like highlands draw on highland, canyon and steppe cultures, not Middle Eastern ones.
  10. Fairy Forest is a magical woodland town. It is the Magicians' historic home and the new home of the Children of the Tree.
  11. Cavelor was founded by ancient guardians. Its people still carry the duty of watching over the Balrog's prison.
  12. The Great World Tree Expedition took place 50 years ago. It found the Children of the Tree and Cavelor, and accidentally damaged the Balrog's seal.
  13. The weakening seal makes the wilderness ever more dangerous. This is the core explanation for the aggressive monsters across Veligor.
  14. The kingdom stays peaceful despite the monsters. The danger is in the land and the wilds, not between its peoples.
  15. The player belongs to Wonder Kingdom from the start. The player character was born and raised here.
  16. The Balrog is the overarching ancient threat. Its true nature, intentions and fate are not yet fully decided.
  17. The world is mostly bright, colorful, prosperous and adventurous. Dark places and dangerous creatures exist, but they do not define everyday life in the kingdom.
  18. Not every story is about the Balrog. The world has ordinary lives, personal adventures, local traditions and mysteries of its own.
  19. Veligor is the starting point, not necessarily the whole world. Other islands and kingdoms may come later.
  20. Undecided details stay undecided. New lore should be clear about what is established and what is only a proposal, rather than quietly adding new canon. On these pages, open questions are kept in Design notes boxes.

The Age of Division The Savages and Magicians fight the Commons and Aristocrats for generations. The Balrog War The Balrog attacks Veligor, and the four peoples unite against it. The Founding The Balrog is defeated and sealed beneath the World Tree. The founding treaty creates Wonder Kingdom, and guardians stay below to found Cavelor. The Age of Unity The kingdom prospers, its towns grow, and the old divisions fade away. 100 years ago Urbanograd is founded and grows its own counterculture. 50 years ago The Great World Tree Expedition finds the Children of the Tree and Cavelor. 50 years ago The expedition accidentally opens a rift that damages the Balrog's seal. The following decades The Age of Disturbance: the Balrog's influence spreads, and the wilderness grows ever more dangerous. Today Wonder Kingdom is united and prosperous, monsters roam much of the wilderness, and the Balrog's prison keeps weakening.

docs.title: Veligor
docs.text:
Veligor is a large island and the home of Wonder Kingdom. Its land is wonderfully varied: fertile plains, high mountains, enchanted forests, long coastlines, quiet farmland, ancient ruins, deep caverns and wide stretches of wilderness.

Near its center rises the enormous World Tree, visible from much of the island and one of its best-known landmarks.

Roads, footpaths and trade routes link the island's towns. The wilds between them have grown dangerous, but the towns themselves are as lively, busy and prosperous as ever, and each has a character all its own.

docs.title: Towns
docs.text:
Town Known as Character Selsior The City of Everything The bustling, joyful capital Kaldemor The Town of Joyful Craftsmanship A cheerful pastoral town of makers and farmers Midbarium The Highland Settlement A rural highland town of clans and chieftains Fairy Forest The Magical Woodland A forest settlement with Magician roots Urbanograd The Town of Societal Rebels A century-old home of free spirits Bain Harbour The Coastal Town A lively, prosperous port Goa Harbour The Wilderness Harbour A rustic port on the far coast Cavelor The Underground City of Guardians The hidden city beneath the World Tree

Beyond Veligor

Veligor is where the story begins, not necessarily the whole world. Other islands and kingdoms may appear later.

docs.title: The World Tree
docs.text: At the heart of Veligor stands the World Tree, one of the island's great landmarks in every sense: geographic, historical and magical. It is no ordinary tree. Its size is staggering, and inside it lie vast worlds of their own, reaching both up into its crown and down into the earth.

docs.title: The Upper World Tree
docs.text:
High in the Tree lie great chambers, ancient branches, strange magical plants and whole ecosystems found nowhere else, home to wondrous magical creatures.

This was the home of the Children of the Tree. The people of the surface knew almost nothing of them until the expedition fifty years ago. Since then, many of the Children have moved to Fairy Forest.

docs.title: The Lower World Tree
docs.text:
Below the ground, the Tree's roots run deep, carving passages through ancient caverns and buried places. The hidden city of Cavelor lies down here.

Deeper still is the Balrog's prison.

docs.title: The Ancient Seal
docs.text:
When the four united peoples defeated the Balrog, they bound it beneath the World Tree with a seal made from powerful magic and the combined strength of the whole alliance. For generations it held.

So the World Tree has two faces. It is a source of natural beauty, magical wonder and extraordinary life, and in its deepest roots it holds the greatest ancient danger Wonder Kingdom has ever known.

docs.title: Bain Harbour
docs.text:
The Coastal Town

Bain Harbour is a prosperous port on one coast of Veligor. It feels like a little of Selsior and a little of Kaldemor, with town life, cheerful craftsmanship and busy trade all meeting the sea.

docs.title: Environment and Identity
docs.text: Bain Harbour is a town of docks and waterfront houses, markets and shipwrights' workshops, and everything travelers and traders need. Its look and spirit blend city and countryside. It is welcoming, prosperous and always sociable.

docs.title: Independence
docs.text:
Bain Harbour is not Selsior's port, nor Kaldemor's. It is a town in its own right, with its own history, people and identity. What it shares with those towns is a feeling, not a chain of command, and it belongs to Wonder Kingdom on equal terms with every other settlement.

It lies on the opposite side of the island from Goa Harbour. The two ports are very different, but they are friends, not rivals.

docs.title: Cavelor
docs.text:
The Underground City of Guardians

Cavelor is a small and very old city hidden deep beneath the World Tree. It was founded right after the first war against the Balrog, when some of the greatest warriors and guardians of that age chose to stay below and keep watch over the seal.

docs.title: Origins
docs.text: The first guardians knew that beating the Balrog had not ended the danger for good. So they stayed beside its prison and kept watch. Over the generations their descendants turned that vigil into a home, with houses, halls, roads, traditions and institutions made for life beneath Veligor.

docs.title: Cultural Identity
docs.text:
Cavelor's people live by responsibility, vigilance, discipline and endurance. They keep the traditions of the first guardians and guard the records of the Balrog, the ancient battle and the magic that holds the prison shut.

Their duty is a solemn one, but Cavelor is not a gloomy or oppressive place. Its people have built a real community with a life of its own.

docs.title: Rediscovery
docs.text: For generations, Cavelor had almost no contact with the rest of the kingdom. Then, fifty years ago, the Great World Tree Expedition reached its halls and met its people, reconnecting the hidden city with the world above. Cavelor is still very much its own place, but it is part of the same united kingdom.

docs.title: Fairy Forest
docs.text:
The Magical Woodland

Fairy Forest is a settlement hidden among ancient trees, where enchanted plants grow, strange creatures wander and the air hums with magic. It is the historic home of the Magicians, one of the four founding peoples.

docs.title: Environment and Culture
docs.text: The people of Fairy Forest live close to both magic and nature. Magical learning, care for the living forest and the study of supernatural wonders are at the heart of who they are. The settlement does not stand apart from the woods; its homes and gathering places are woven into the forest itself.

docs.title: The Children of the Tree
docs.text:
Fifty years ago, the Great World Tree Expedition found a mysterious people of magical beings living high in the upper reaches of the World Tree. They came to be known as the Children of the Tree.

After that first meeting, the Children slowly came down from the Tree and settled in Fairy Forest. They have since become part of its community and made friends across the kingdom, and their presence gives the forest much of its unique magic.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by MapleStory's Ellinia. The nature, appearance, abilities and origins of the Children of the Tree are still to be decided.

docs.title: Goa Harbour
docs.text:
The Wilderness Harbour

Goa Harbour is a port on the far side of Veligor from Bain Harbour. It feels like a little of Midbarium and a little of Fairy Forest, with highland ruggedness and woodland magic meeting the sea.

docs.title: Environment and Identity
docs.text: Goa Harbour is rougher and wilder than Bain Harbour, shaped by the mountains, forests and rocky shores around it. Its people keep proud seafaring traditions, along with the independent spirit and touch of magic of the neighboring regions. It is an adventurous, welcoming place unlike any other town on the island.

docs.title: Independence
docs.text:
Goa Harbour is not Midbarium's port, nor Fairy Forest's. It has its own people, traditions and history, and its resemblance to those towns is cultural, not political.

Bain Harbour and Goa Harbour are not rivals. Both are peaceful, prosperous parts of Wonder Kingdom.

docs.title: Kaldemor
docs.text:
The Town of Joyful Craftsmanship

Kaldemor is a cheerful pastoral town set among fertile fields, rolling hills and green countryside. Its heart is joyful craftsmanship: its people love making things with their own hands, growing their own food and living well together.

docs.title: Architecture and Environment
docs.text: Kaldemor is a town of colorful wooden houses and cozy cottages, workshops and gardens, barns and welcoming village greens. Beyond it stretch meadows, farmland, orchards, gentle hills and patches of woodland. It is a sunny, colorful place that seems to invite visitors in.

docs.title: Culture and Atmosphere
docs.text:
The people of Kaldemor value creativity, practical know-how, friendliness, cooperation and the quiet satisfaction of work done well. Traditional crafts are part of everyday life: woodworking, carpentry, pottery and farming all shape who the town is.

Kaldemor is no poor backwater. It is a prosperous, happy town whose people love the life they have made. Where Selsior stands for the excitement and variety of the great city, Kaldemor stands for the joy of creating, growing and belonging to a close-knit community.

In the game

Kaldemor is in the game today. See Kaldemor in the world guide for its maps, NPCs, quests and hunting grounds.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by the bright, welcoming character of MapleStory's Henesys.

docs.title: Midbarium
docs.text:
The Highland Settlement

Midbarium is a rugged, rural mountain town and the ancestral home of the Savages' culture. It sits high in Veligor's dry uplands, among red-rock peaks, sheer cliffs, deep canyons and steep highland trails, and its people grew strong learning to live with them.

docs.title: The Land
docs.text:
The highlands around Midbarium are a hard, beautiful country. Rain is scarce, the sun is fierce, and the wind carries red dust down the canyons for days at a time. Above the town rise wind-carved mesas and bare stone spires; below it, dry riverbeds wind through rocky valleys dotted with caves, hardy scrub and the odd twisted tree. Nights are cold and clear, and the stars over the plateau are famous across the kingdom.

Life here follows the land. There are no grand fields like Kaldemor's. Instead, families farm small stone terraces on the slopes, watered by springs and carefully kept cisterns, and they drive herds of goats and other hardy beasts between the high pastures and the valley floors as the seasons turn. Many Midbarians live not in the town itself but in scattered homesteads and camps across the highlands, coming in to trade, to settle disputes and to celebrate.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Midbarium is built into the mountainside. Its houses are thick-walled and earthen-red, made of stone and sun-dried clay that keep out the heat of the day and hold warmth through the night. Heavy timber beams carry the roofs of the great halls, and terraces, carved stairways and swaying rope-and-plank bridges join the levels of the town across the cliffs.

Out in the highlands, herding families live in sturdy hide tents and stone shelters that can be moved or rebuilt with the seasons. Painted standards and carved totems mark the camps of each clan.

docs.title: The Clans and Their Chieftains
docs.text:
Midbarium is not governed like Selsior. Its people belong to clans, large families bound by blood, oath and shared history, and each clan follows a chieftain.

A chieftain is not simply born to the role. They are chosen for their strength, wisdom and fairness, and they are expected to lead from the front: to walk the hardest trail first, to judge disputes fairly, to protect the herds and to look after the weakest members of the clan. A chieftain who forgets this does not stay chieftain for long.

When matters affect the whole town, the chieftains meet in council at the great hall, around a fire that, by tradition, is never allowed to go out. Decisions are argued long and loudly, but once the council agrees, every clan stands by it. Within Wonder Kingdom, the council speaks for Midbarium, and the chieftains are as loyal to the kingdom as any lord in the capital.

docs.title: Culture and Atmosphere
docs.text:
Midbarium stands for strength, resilience, independence and respect for the ancestors. Its people admire anyone who overcomes hardship, and they guard the knowledge handed down by earlier generations: the old paths through the canyons, where water can be found in a dry year, and the stories of the clans.

Hospitality is sacred in the highlands, where a traveler turned away might not survive the night. Anyone who comes to a Midbarian fire in peace is given water, food and a place to sleep, no questions asked. Feasts, storytelling, contests of strength and long nights of drumming and song mark the clans' gatherings.

For all its rugged looks, Midbarium is not hostile, primitive or grim, and it holds nothing against outsiders. Today it is a peaceful, welcoming town whose people are proud of both their ancestral traditions and their place in Wonder Kingdom.

Design notes

The geography and look are inspired by MapleStory's Perion. Midbarium is rural and mountainous, ruled by clan chieftains, with a dry highland and desert feel. It should draw on highland, canyon and steppe cultures, not on Middle Eastern or Arabian desert cultures. The names of the clans, the number of chieftains and how the council chooses its speaker are still open.

docs.title: Selsior
docs.text:
The City of Everything

Selsior is the capital of Wonder Kingdom and by far the largest city on Veligor. It is a bustling fantasy metropolis: crowded, noisy, endlessly busy and remarkably diverse. People call it the City of Everything, and they mean it. Its residents trade, craft, teach, study, perform, govern and do a thousand other things besides, in marketplaces and workshops, schools and theatres, taverns and quiet residential lanes.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Selsior is a classic medieval fantasy city. Timber-framed houses stand on stone foundations under brightly colored roofs, towers rise over the skyline, and cobblestone streets run between the neighborhoods.

At its heart lie broad avenues, great public squares and the city's most important civic spaces. Around them sprawl dense old quarters that grew without a plan: winding streets, narrow passages, hidden courtyards, crowded homes and little local markets.

docs.title: Culture and Atmosphere
docs.text:
Selsior is cheerful, sociable and full of energy. Street performers draw crowds on every corner, festivals fill the squares, and there always seems to be something to celebrate. The city is busy not only because people work there, but because its people love city life and throw themselves into it.

Folk from every corner of Wonder Kingdom live side by side in Selsior, and nobody thinks that strange. More than anywhere else, the capital shows what the founding of the kingdom achieved: prosperity, cooperation and a shared identity, with room for every kind of life and ambition.

In the game

Selsior is in the game today. See Selsior in the world guide for its maps, NPCs and shops.

Design notes

Classic medieval fantasy architecture. Joyful, bustling and cosmopolitan.

docs.title: Urbanograd
docs.text:
The Town of Societal Rebels

Urbanograd is a city unlike any other on Veligor. It was founded 100 years ago, long after the four peoples had united, so its identity has nothing to do with the old wars. It grew up inside the kingdom, built by people who wanted to live their own way: free to express themselves and free of the expectations of ordinary society. Over the century since, it has grown a counterculture all its own.

docs.title: Cultural Identity
docs.text:
Urbanograd is famous as the home of societal rebels. Its people prize individuality, creativity, unconventional thinking, free expression and the right to live differently. The city draws anyone who loves alternative lifestyles and unusual art, music and fashion.

But its people are not revolutionaries. They have no wish to unsettle the kingdom, topple its institutions or quarrel with their neighbors. Their rebellion is cultural and personal, not political.

docs.title: Relationship with Wonder Kingdom
docs.text:
Urbanograd is a full and proud part of Wonder Kingdom. Its people respect the kingdom and get along well with every other community, and the rest of Veligor accepts the city's unusual character. Its people are understood, not distrusted.

Urbanograd shows that the kingdom's founding promise reaches further than peace between the original four peoples. Wonder Kingdom also welcomes communities that invent entirely new ways of living.

Design notes

The atmosphere is inspired by MapleStory's Kerning City.

Town Guide

Where Kaldemor Services Quests

Welcome to Kaldemor, Player!

docs.title: Says
docs.text:
• "New in town? Ask me anything!"
  • "Press Space near someone to talk to them."
  • "The market is just east of here."

docs.title: Quests
docs.text:
• Welcome Home (gives)
Dialogue
  • Hi, Player! I show newcomers around Kaldemor. Ask me anything!
    • Choice: Where am I?
    • Choice: What is there to do here?
    • Choice: Anything new in town?
    • Choice: Am I ready for the fields?
    • Choice: How do I...?
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Of course! What would you like to know?
    • Choice: ...move and fight?
    • Choice: ...see how strong I am?
    • Choice: ...learn and use skills?
    • Choice: ...carry and wear things?
    • Choice: ...keep track of my quests?
    • Choice: Never mind.
  • Walk with the arrow keys and jump with Alt. Up takes a portal or climbs a ladder, and Down with Alt drops through a ledge.
  • Swing with Ctrl, pick up what monsters leave behind with Z, and talk to people with Space or a click. Every key can be changed with the backslash key.
  • Press S to open your stat window: your level, HP and MP, and the strength, dexterity and the rest that decide how hard you hit.
  • Every level gives you ability points to spend there. A warrior puts most of them into STR.
  • Press K for your skills. Each level from the second one gives you skill points, and a click on the + puts one into a skill.
  • A skill has a key of its own, and costs MP each time you use it. Blue potions bring the MP back.
  • Press I for your inventory: four tabs, one for what you wear, drink, collect and sit on. Double-click a potion to drink it.
  • Press E for what you wear: double-click a piece of equipment to put it on, and a worn one to take it off.
  • Press Q for your quest log: what you can take up, what you are doing, and what you have done. Pick a quest to read its story and its rewards.
  • The quests you follow are listed on the right of the screen with how far you are. Click one to open it in the log.
  • This is the town square of Kaldemor. The big treehouse behind us is the oldest building in town.
  • The people here are friendly. Say hello to everyone: press Space near someone, or click them!
  • Visit the Market to the east for potions and gear. When you feel strong, the fields beyond the town are full of monsters to practice on.
  • People with a light bulb over their head have a job for you. Helping them is a good way to learn your way around!
  • Oh, yes! The clock tower in the park has stopped. Nobody can say when it will tick again.
  • Old Ewan, the clockkeeper, has been up there for days. Maybe he would like some company.
  • You carry (how many you carry) Red Potions - good. Snails nibble, and a potion mends it. Drink one with its key before it gets serious!
  • I would take some Red Potions along first: you carry (how many you carry). Bram sells them in the market, east of here.
  • Have fun, Player!

  • I drill those who want to be tested, Player. Spikes, rocks, platforms that will not wait for you, and a yard full of things that bite. What will it be?
    • Choice: What is the Gauntlet?
    • Choice: I want to run the Kaldemor Gauntlet.
    • Choice: I want to run the Kaldemor Gauntlet.

  • Three stages, one after the other. First the yard: whatever I turn loose, you beat down. Then the hanging course: gather the star shards and reach the far ledge before the clock runs out. Then the last stand: hold out for a full minute.
  • Fall, flee or run out of time, and it is over. Come back and I will send you in again, no waiting. Potions are allowed. Scrolls are not.
  • Not yet, Player. Come back at level 10 and I will put you through it.

  • Level one hundred and twenty, Player. Speak to me again and I will set you the last trial.

  • Ah, Player, the one who found my spores! Come in, come in, wipe your boots.
  • Player! I saved you the heel of the loaf, it is the best part. Sit a moment, the oven is warm.
  • My dear Player, there you are. The bakery is as much yours as mine, you know. Take what you like.
  • Welcome to my bakery, Player! What can I do for you?

  • Bread, mostly: round loaves, long loaves, and my mushroom bread, which the whole town swears by. The terrace oven has not gone cold in years.
  • The secret is in the spores. Do not tell anyone I said so.
  • Oh, it is lively! Half the market comes up my steps before noon, and the other half comes after.
  • Oh, it is lively! And half of them ask after you, Player. You have a name in Kaldemor now, did you know? The mayor's own bread comes from this oven.
  • You want the oven's story? My grandmother built it with her own hands, brick by brick, the year the clock tower was raised. She said a bakery without a warm oven is only a shop.

Dialogue
  • Ah, Player! Lia told you about the clock tower, did she? Old Ewan has been fretting about it for days.
  • Welcome to Kaldemor, the greenest town this side of the old forest. What can I do for you?
    • Choice: Tell me about Kaldemor.
    • Choice: Who are you?
    • Choice: Guess how many people live here.
    • Choice: Nothing, thanks.
  • Kaldemor grew up around the great treehouse behind me. The mushroom houses came later - the soil here grows them big enough to live in!
  • West of the square is the Park, with the clock tower and the old windmill farm. East is the Market: potions, weapons, bread, all of it.
  • Walk through the glowing portals with the up arrow to go between them.
  • I'm Tobin, mayor of this town for thirty years now. Would you like to hear how Kaldemor began?
  • Long ago a traveller planted a single seed in this meadow and slept under it for a night. In the morning it was a tree taller than a tower.
  • People came to see it, and some never left. That traveller's name is lost, but we still say: every great town starts with one seed.
  • Another time, then. Old men always have time for stories.
  • A guess, is it? Go on: how many people live in Kaldemor, would you say?
  • N, you say? Not bad, Player! There are just under three hundred of us - not counting the snails.
  • Take care out there, Player. Come back any time!

docs.title: A Head for Heights
docs.text:
Garrick the climber will teach Rope Up to anyone who can reach the lookout on the high ledge of Kaldemor Hills by the vine on its west side.

Category Side Given by Garrick Level 3 After Settling In

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach the hills' lookout in Kaldemor Hills

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 150 EXP
  • Skill: Rope Up
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • You climbed my ladder to get up here, so you have the hands for it. I have a trick that spares you the climb: Rope Up, a leap that throws you onto the rope or ledge above.
  • But I teach only those who have seen the world from above. Climb the long vine on the west side of Kaldemor Hills, as far as the lookout on its high ledge, then come back to me.
  • The hills are west of the town square. The vine is long, and the grass up there is soft if you slip.
  • Heights are not for everyone. The offer stands.
  • The lookout is at the top of the long vine on the west side of Kaldemor Hills, Player. Climb up, look around, then come back.
  • Ha! You have the look of someone who has seen the clouds up close. Right: bend your knees, look up, and let go.
  • That is Rope Up. Open the skills window with K, find it on the Beginner tab and drag it onto a key; Page Down is its key until you move it. It throws you up to the nearest rope or ledge above, so mind the ceilings.

  • Would you go to Bram, in the Market, and tell him the oven is warm for him? That is all. He will understand.
  • Thank you, dear. Take the portal east of the square, his stall is at the far end of the Market.
  • Of course. It has waited years, it can wait a little more.
  • Bram is at the far end of the Market, Player. Tell him the oven is warm.
  • Rosa said that? The oven is warm, for me? Well, well. Tell her I will come by for a loaf, and that I was the stubborn one.
  • He said he will come? Oh, Player. I could hug you, and I will, as soon as I take this tray out.
  • Here, a few Orange Potions for your trouble. You have given me more than that.

docs.title: A Sharper Sword
docs.text:
Gareth the smith gives you a Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT. Use it on a one-handed sword: drag the scroll from the Use tab onto the sword, worn (equipment window) or carried (Equip tab). A sword is on sale in his shop.

Category Side Given by Gareth Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Use Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT 100%

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60 EXP
  • Scroll for One-Handed Sword for ATT 100% x1
Dialogue
  • A good smith never stops at the first blow, Player. A blade can be sharpened with a scroll: it adds to its attack, and each scroll takes one of the sword's upgrade slots for good. I will give you one for a one-handed sword. Use it on yours, and I will give you a second to keep. If you have no sword, there is one on my shelf.
  • Here is the scroll. Drag it from your Use tab onto the sword, worn or in your bag. Careful: the sword only has so many slots.
  • Another day, then. The scroll will keep.
  • Drag the scroll from your Use tab onto a one-handed sword. If you have none, I sell a plain Sword.
  • There, it bites deeper now. Keep this second scroll for the next sword, and here is something for your trouble.

docs.title: A Smith's First Bar
docs.text:
Gareth the smith will show you the forge's first lesson: strike 4 copper ore from the veins in the fields, then smelt it into a copper ingot (open the Professions window and make it).

Category Side Given by Gareth Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 4 Copper Ore
  2. Make 1 Copper Ingot

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Recipe: Bronze Axe (Smithing)
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Bring me a bar, Player, and I will teach you more than a shopkeeper ever could. The fields are full of copper veins: stand by one and press the gather key, a few blows and it gives. Strike 4 copper ore, then smelt a copper ingot from it in your Professions window. Do that and I will teach you the bronze axe.
  • Good. The veins glitter in the east and west fields. They fill again after a while, so there is always more.
  • The forge will keep. Come back when your arms itch for it.
  • Four copper ore from the veins, then an ingot from the ore. Press the gather key by a vein.
  • A fine first bar! Copper is soft, but every smith starts there.
  • Here is your pay, and the bronze axe: its recipe is yours now. Bronze takes a little more skill, but you have the hands for it.

docs.title: A Steady Brew
docs.text:
Bram the potion seller will show you how a potion is brewed: pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields, then brew 2 red potions from them (open the Professions window and make them).

Category Side Given by Bram Level 5 After A Pot for Rosa

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Gather 4 Marjoram Flower
  2. Make 2 Red Potion

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 180 EXP
  • 200 mesos
  • Recipe: Orange Potion (Alchemy)
  • +15 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Rosa tells me you cook, Player. A brew is only a pot with a better reason. Pick 4 marjoram flowers from the patches in the fields and brew 2 red potions in your Professions window: two flowers and a mushroom spore make one. Do that and I will teach you the orange potion.
  • Marjoram patches dot the east and west fields. Mushroom spores drop from the Shrooms. Do not drink the first batch, mind.
  • No hurry. The cauldron is not going anywhere.
  • Four marjoram flowers, then two red potions: each takes two flowers and a mushroom spore.
  • Two potions, and they do heal. You have the hands for it, Player.
  • Here is your pay, and the orange potion's recipe. It wants lavender, which grows a little deeper in the fields, and the caps of orange mushrooms.

docs.title: The Grand Swordmaster's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Swordmaster of level 120 to the top of the sword's road. Prove it once more in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 400 of its monsters.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 120 Job Swordmaster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 400 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 180,000 EXP
  • Advance to Grand Swordmaster

Placeholder

A stand-in until the higher fields exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the region of level 120 when that is built (IMPL 9.9-9.10).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level one hundred and twenty. I have trained a great many Swordmasters in this yard, and few come back to ask for more.
  • The Grand Swordmaster is not a stronger Swordmaster. He is one who no longer waits for the enemy's blow to begin his own, and who can turn it aside while doing so.
  • One last trial, in the place where you began it: defeat 400 of the Greenwood Clearing's Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps without once letting your rhythm break.
  • Then go. Four hundred is a lot of cuts, so make each one lead into the next.
  • The last step is the longest. Come back when you are ready for it.
  • Four hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player, on the royal road outside the city. Do not let the rhythm break.
  • Four hundred. I watched your cuts from the first to the last, and I could not find the seam between them.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Grand Swordmaster.
  • Blade Tempest, Perfect Counter and Crescent Divide are yours now. Chain them into the Swordmaster's cuts, or fight each by itself: the sword has no wrong way. Use them well.

docs.title: Hale's Bounty
docs.text:
Ranger Hale pays a bounty for thinning out the meadow: defeat 30 of the field's monsters. He will pay it again, any time.

Category Repeatable Given by Hale Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 30 Field monsters (Snail, Blue Snail, Red Snail)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 100 EXP
  • 200 mesos

The first time you complete it instead: 150 EXP, 300 mesos, +30 standing with Kaldemor

Dialogue
  • The meadow is never empty for long, Player. If you have the stomach, I pay a bounty: 30 monsters of the field, snails of any colour, and I pay it again whenever you bring me another thirty. The first time is a little more.
  • Good. The field is east of the town square. Count them as you go: the tracker does it for you.
  • Another time, then. The snails will wait.
  • Thirty of the field's monsters, Player. Snails of any colour count.
  • Thirty! The meadow can breathe again.
  • Here is your bounty. Come back for another round whenever the snails get bold.

docs.title: Rosa's Recipe
docs.text:
Rosa the baker needs 10 Mushroom Spores and 5 Blue Snail Shells for her famous mushroom bread.

Category Side Given by Rosa Level 3

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Bring 10 Mushroom Spore (taken)
  • Bring 5 Blue Snail Shell (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 250 EXP
  • Orange Potion x10
  • +200 standing with Rosa
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Oh, Player, you look like someone who is not afraid of mushrooms! My famous mushroom bread needs spores and a pinch of ground blue shell, and my usual supplier has gone to visit his sister.
  • Bring me 10 Mushroom Spores from the Shrooms in the woods, and 5 Blue Snail Shells from the blue snails in the meadow. I will pay you in Orange Potions.
  • Wonderful! The Shrooms live in the woods, west of the town square past the hills; the blue snails are in the meadow to the east.
  • No harm done, dear. The oven will keep.
  • You carry (how many you carry) of 10 Mushroom Spores and (how many you carry) of 5 Blue Snail Shells so far. Take your time.
  • Spores and shells, and not a one broken! You are a treasure.
  • Here are your Orange Potions, ten of them. Come by any time, Player, the bread is always warm.

docs.title: Settling In
docs.text:
Tobin wants you to see the Market and meet Bram, the potion seller.

Category Story Given by Tobin Completed with Tobin Level 1 After Welcome Home

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach Kaldemor Market
  • Talk to Bram

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 20 EXP
  • Red Potion x5
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • A good traveller knows where to shop. Would you visit the Market, east of the square, and say hello to Bram, the potion seller? Tell him I sent you.
  • Thank you, Player! Take the glowing portal on the east side with the up arrow. Bram's stall is at the far end of the Market.
  • Of course, of course. Come back whenever you like.
  • Have you been to the Market yet? Bram's stall is at the far end. Take the portal east of the square.
  • Oh, Tobin sent you? Welcome, Player! Come back to me whenever you need potions. Tell the mayor that Bram says hello!
  • You met Bram? Splendid! I knew you would fit right in.
  • Please take these Red Potions. They will keep you going out in the fields. Good luck, Player!

docs.title: Shells for the Mayor
docs.text:
Mayor Tobin collects snail shells for the new fence. Bring him 15 Green Snail Shells.

Category Story Given by Hale Completed with Tobin Level 2 After Snail Trouble

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Bring 15 Green Snail Shell (taken)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 120 EXP
  • Wooden Buckler x1
  • +30 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Well done with the snails, Player. Funny thing: the mayor wants their shells to grind into the mortar for the new fence. Would you bring 15 Green Snail Shells to Tobin? They drop from the green snails now and then.
  • Good. Pick up what the snails leave behind with Z, and carry the shells to Tobin in the town square.
  • Fair enough. The shells will keep, and so will I.
  • Fifteen Green Snail Shells for Tobin. You carry (how many you carry) so far.
  • Shells! Splendid, and so many of them. Hale told me you were reliable, Player.
  • Take this Wooden Buckler for your trouble. A fighter needs something to hold in the other hand.

docs.title: Snail Trouble
docs.text:
Snails are eating the town's gardens. Thin them out in the meadow, then see Ranger Hale at the park gate.

Category Story Given by Tobin Completed with Hale Level 2 After Settling In

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 10 Snail

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 60 EXP
  • 100 mesos
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Ah, Player, just the one I wanted! The snails are back in the gardens and eat everything they can reach. Would you thin them out? Defeat 10 Snails in the meadow east of the square, then see Hale, the ranger at the park gate.
  • Thank you, Player! The meadow is through the portal on the east side of the square. Hale will be waiting at the park gate.
  • Another day, then. The snails are not going anywhere. That is rather the problem.
  • Still at it? Ten Snails, in the meadow east of the square. Then Hale at the park gate will see you right.
  • Mayor Tobin said you would come! Ten snails, and the gardens will be quiet for a week.
  • Here is your pay, Player. You have the makings of a fine hunter.

docs.title: Strength of a Warrior
docs.text:
Tobin says a warrior is measured by more than errands. Reach level 5 and use Power Strike five times. He will teach you Warrior's Resolve.

Category Story Given by Tobin Level 3 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Reach level 5
  • Use Power Strike 5 times

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 200 EXP
  • Bronze Helmet x1
  • Skill: Warrior's Resolve
  • +20 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Player, I have watched you grow these past days. Snails, shells, errands: not bad for a newcomer. But a warrior is measured by more than errands.
  • Put your points to work. Reach level 5, and learn the Power Strike: open the skill window with K, spend a skill point on it, and use it 5 times on whatever gets in your way.
  • Skill points go into your skills in the K window, and ability points into your stats in the S window. Come back when you have done both, Player.
  • Strength can wait a little. Come back when you feel ready.
  • Level 5 and five Power Strikes, Player. Press K if you have not spent your skill points yet; the strike sits on Shift until you move it.
  • Level 5, and a Power Strike that makes the snails think twice! I knew you had it in you.
  • Take this Bronze Helmet. Keep your head covered and your chin down, and it will serve you well. And take something I cannot wrap: Warrior's Resolve, a battle cry that hardens you for three minutes. It is on the Beginner tab of the skills window; drag it onto a key, or press F1.

docs.title: The Sword Saint's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Grand Swordmaster of level 160 beyond the Guard's ranks, to the Sword Saint. Prove your edge in the Greenwood Clearing: defeat 600 of its monsters.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 160 Job Grand Swordmaster

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 600 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 600,000 EXP
  • Advance to Sword Saint

Placeholder

A stand-in until the fields past level 120 exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the far fields when they are built (IMPL Phase 14).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level one hundred and sixty. I have no rank left to give you, and I am told there is one beyond all of them.
  • The old Guard called it the Sword Saint: one for whom the sword is no longer carried but followed, who cuts the sky open and lets a thousand blades answer.
  • I can only set you the old test: defeat 600 of the Greenwood Clearing's Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps, and show me that the road has nothing left to teach you.
  • Then go. Six hundred, and each cut leading into the next.
  • Few ask twice. Come back when the sword calls you.
  • Six hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player, on the royal road outside the city.
  • Six hundred. I stopped counting the cuts at two hundred and began to watch your blade instead; it no longer seemed to hold you.
  • Kneel, Player, one last time. By the old authority of the Guard, I name you a Sword Saint.
  • Heavenly Severance and Infinite Blade Dance are yours now. Chain them into the cuts you know, as the sword wills. Use them well.

docs.title: The Swordmaster's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Swordsman of level 70 into the Swordmaster's way. Prove it with a long hunt in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 200 of its monsters.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 70 Job Swordsman

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Defeat 200 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 40,000 EXP
  • Advance to Swordmaster

Placeholder

A stand-in until the higher fields exist: it asks for the strongest monsters there are today, the Greenwood Clearing's. Its hunt moves to the region of level 70 when that is built (IMPL 9.4-9.5).

Dialogue
  • Player. Level seventy, and still the same steady arm. The Guard has a name for those who get this far: Swordmaster.
  • A Swordmaster does not end a cut. He lets it run into the next, and the next after it. That cannot be taught on a practice dummy, only in a long fight that does not let up.
  • Go back to the Greenwood Clearing, on the royal road outside the city, and defeat 200 of its Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps. They are the toughest creatures the Guard can set you against today. Cut them down one after another, and do not stop between cuts.
  • Good. It is a long hunt, so bring potions and patience. Come back when the count is full.
  • A long road needs a steady start. Come back when you are ready.
  • Two hundred of the Greenwood's monsters, Player. The clearing is on the royal road, outside the city. Keep cutting.
  • Two hundred, and your guard never dropped. That is the rhythm I was looking for.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Swordmaster.
  • Four new cuts are yours: Flash Cutter, Blade Cyclone, Thousand Cuts and Rising Blade. Press one while another is still finishing, and it takes over at once. Use them well.

docs.title: The Swordsman's Trial
docs.text:
Captain Rhys will take a Warrior of level 30 into the Swordsman's way. Prove it in the Greenwood Clearing on the royal road: defeat 30 of its monsters and bring back 5 trial seals.

Category Story Given by Rhys Level 30 Job Warrior

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
• Defeat 30 Greenwood monsters (Horny Mushroom, Axe Stump)
  • Deliver 5 Guard's Trial Seal

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 4,000 EXP
  • Advance to Swordsman
Dialogue
  • Player. Level thirty, and a steady arm. I have been waiting to say this: you are ready for the Guard's trial.
  • A Swordsman does not swing harder. He swings truer. That is learned where the fight is real, not on a practice dummy.
  • Go to the Greenwood Clearing, on the royal road outside the city. Defeat 30 of the Horny Mushrooms and Axe Stumps there, and bring me 5 Guard's Trial Seals. The Guard stamps a seal on a leaf, and those creatures carry them off while you are on trial.
  • Good. Mind the Axe Stumps: they hit harder than they look. Keep your potions close, and come back when it is done.
  • A sword that is not ready is worse than no sword. Come back when you are.
  • Thirty of the Greenwood's monsters and five trial seals, Player. The clearing is on the royal road, outside the city.
  • Five seals, and the clearing quieter for it. I watched for a steady arm, and here it is.
  • Kneel, Player. By the authority of the Royal Guard, I name you a Swordsman.
  • Your cuts will come quicker and truer from now on: the Swordsman's attacks are yours. Use them well.

docs.title: The Clock Stopped
docs.text:
The clock tower in the park has stopped. Old Ewan thinks a Shroom took its gear: hunt 20 Shrooms, then bring the gear back.

Category Story Given by Ewan Level 4 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text:
1. Defeat 20 Shroom
  2. Deliver 1 Clock Gear

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 400 EXP
  • Old Pocket Watch x1
  • +50 standing with Kaldemor
  • Sets kaldemor.clock_running
Dialogue
  • Ah, a visitor! Mind the dust. I am Ewan, keeper of this clock these forty years, and this morning it stopped.
  • The works are not broken. A gear is missing: the great gear, and I would swear a Shroom from the woods dragged it off in the night. They take anything shiny.
  • Thin out 20 Shrooms in the woods, past the hills west of the town square, and bring me my Clock Gear. One of them will have it, I am sure.
  • Thank you, Player. When the Shrooms are fewer, the gear will turn up: bring it straight here. The whole town will thank you when the bell rings again.
  • I understand, it is a long walk. The clock will be here. Not ticking, but here.
  • Twenty Shrooms first, then the gear. The woods are west of the town square, past the hills.
  • My gear! Oh, look at it, not a scratch. Give me a moment...
  • There. Do you hear that? Tick, tick, tick. Kaldemor has its time back.
  • Please take my old pocket watch. It never stopped once in forty years, and I hope it brings you luck.

docs.title: The Snail King
docs.text:
Ranger Hale has heard something huge in a hollow beyond the woods. Walk to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge past the hills, and tell him what you find.

Category Story Given by Hale Level 12 After Shells for the Mayor

docs.title: Objectives
docs.text: • Reach Kaldemor Woods

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 300 EXP
  • +40 standing with Kaldemor
  • Unlocks boss.snail_king
Dialogue
  • You are not the newcomer who carried shells for the mayor any more, Player. So I will tell you what I have not told the others: something huge has settled in a hollow past Kaldemor Woods. The snails do not stray that way now, and the ground shakes at night.
  • I need someone to walk out to Kaldemor Woods, the forest edge beyond the hills, and tell me whether the road to it is clear. If it is, I can show you the way to the hollow myself. Will you go?
  • Good. The woods are west of the town, past the hills. Bring potions, Player: whatever sleeps out there is no snail of the meadow.
  • Wise to be sure of yourself. Come back when you are.
  • Kaldemor Woods, Player: west of the town, past the hills. Walk to it and come back to tell me it is clear.
  • You made it there and back, and you are in one piece. Then it is as I thought: the old giant snail Mano has taken the hollow, and it has called itself a king.
  • Whenever you are ready, ask me and I will take you to the Snail King's hollow. Mind the red marks on the ground: they show where it will land. And remember: no scroll will get you out of there.

docs.title: Welcome Home
docs.text:
Lia says the mayor wants to meet you. Go and see Tobin.

Category Story Given by Lia Completed with Tobin Level 1

docs.title: Rewards
docs.text:
• 15 EXP
  • +10 standing with Kaldemor
Dialogue
  • Oh, a new face! Welcome to Kaldemor, Player. Mayor Tobin wants to meet every newcomer. Would you go and see him? He is just west of here.
  • Wonderful! Tobin is the mayor, standing in front of the treehouse. Just walk up to him and talk.
  • No rush. If you change your mind, I am right here.
  • Mayor Tobin is waiting for you, Player. He is just to the west.
  • Ah, you must be Player! Lia told me about you. Welcome to Kaldemor, my dear. I hope you will call it home.
  • Take this as a welcome gift. Come and talk to me again when you are ready for more.

docs.text:
Runs are staged challenges entered through an NPC.

Run Stages Kaldemor Gauntlet 3

docs.text:

Dying ends the run.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Skill numbers come from formulas of the skill level; each table below works them out level by level.

Skill Group Kind Max level Description Power Strike Warrior Attack 20 A strong strike at one enemy in front. Sweeping Slash Warrior Attack 20 A wide slash that sweeps the enemies in front. Ground Breaker Warrior Attack 20 A heavy double slash at the enemies in front. War Leap Warrior Leap 10 Dash far through the air the way you face: jump again in the air, or press its key. Triple Slash Swordsman Attack 20 Three quick cuts at the enemies in front. Blade Wave Swordsman Projectile 20 Sends a blade of force flying ahead, cutting every enemy in its way once. Counter Slash Swordsman Counter 20 Hold a guard: the first attack or touch that would land on you meanwhile is turned aside, and you strike back hard. With nothing to turn aside it does nothing. Sword Dash Swordsman Dash 20 Dash along the ground, cutting every enemy you pass through once. It stops at a wall or the edge of a ledge. Flash Cutter Swordmaster Attack 20 Two lightning cuts in front, cheap and quick. The start of most chains. Blade Cyclone Swordmaster Attack 20 Spin with the blade out and cut everything around you, over and over. Thousand Cuts Swordmaster Attack 20 A storm of cuts too quick to count, on every enemy in front. Rising Blade Swordmaster Attack 20 Carries you up on a rising cut, hitting everything above you on the way. A good way into the air, and to the next chain. docs.text:

From the top of the long vine the whole of the western hills lies below you. Far off in the woods one birch stands taller than the rest, and a squirrel keeps vanishing behind it.

docs.text:
Region Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Park Size Common Reward 25 EXP What you see

From the climbers' ledge you stand level with the clock tower's face. The hands are stuck, and the gears behind the glass look like they only need a patient hand.

docs.text:
Region Kaldemor Where Kaldemor Woods Size Rare Reward 40 EXP, 250 mesos, Red Potion x5 What you see

Behind the woods' birch a hollow in the trunk held a tin box, wrapped in oilcloth, that some traveller hid long ago. The squirrel had been guarding it.

docs.title: The Crossing's Hilltop
docs.text:
Region The Royal Road Where The Crossing Size Common Reward 25 EXP, 150 mesos What you see

From the gazebo's hill both roads show at once: the royal road running west to the capital, and the narrow path that leaves it for the Greenwood.

docs.title: The Greenwood's Crown
docs.text:
Region The Royal Road Where Greenwood Clearing Size Rare Reward 40 EXP, Orange Potion x3 What you see

The crown ledge above the clearing is cut off from the rest by two ladders. Someone has set a log bench here, as if to watch the mushrooms from above.

docs.title: The Skywalk's View
docs.text:
Region Selsior Where Selsior Size Common Reward 25 EXP, 150 mesos What you see

From the skywalk above the plaza the capital spreads out: the Great Bell on its dais, the fountain, and the throne hall's red carpet running up the palace steps.

docs.title: The Great Bell
docs.text:
Region Selsior Where Selsior Size Common Reward 25 EXP What you see

You laid a hand on the Great Bell's rim and it hummed through your arm. The guards say it rings only for coronations, and for no one else.
